question: For the two frozen-A flat-tangent punctured lapse kernels already recorded by the finite m=2 bosonic source pushforward, can C/|N| and the single-sheet C/N differ only by a distribution supported at N=0, and does either punctured kernel have a unique scaling-degree-preserving extension without an added normalization condition?
primary_failure: source-defined joint lapse glue and zero-contact selection

ragnarok_boundary.distinct_question: This audit starts from the already computed frozen-A C/|N| and C/z kernels. It does not evaluate the full Starobinsky q-paired holomorphic amplitude, prove its boundary value, or retry any check from the consumed scalar zero-lapse one-shot.

inherited_only: At frozen A and x=q=0 the independently normalized real-arm kernel is C/|N| with C=sqrt(6)*pi*A^2/hbar.
The transported declared configuration rays give a single holomorphic sheet C/z and hence C/N away from zero on the real boundary.
The negative-arm ratio between that sheet and the real-arm normalization is -1.
No source-to-thimble deformation, determinant-line orientation, zero-lapse distribution, or physical original cycle was established.

primary_sources.title: Microlocal Analysis and Interacting Quantum Field Theories: Renormalization on Physical Backgrounds
primary_sources.role: Theorem 5.2: at scaling degree omega>=d, same-scaling-degree extensions exist and are fixed only after the finite set of point-supported data is supplied; for omega=d=1 the freedom is a delta term.

primary_sources.title: Extension of distributions, scalings and renormalization of QFT on Riemannian manifolds
primary_sources.role: Hadamard finite-part example and the general fact that two extensions differ by a distribution supported on the singular set.

primary_sources.title: On the lapse contour in the gravitational path integral
primary_sources.role: Comparator for the below-origin N-i0 prescription after momentum integration; it is not imported as a derivation of this workbench's joint source cycle, negative-arm determinant glue, or absolute measure.

declared_conventions.local_model: frozen positive A, hbar>0, m=2, x=q=0 flat tangent
declared_conventions.negative_support_probe: psi(N)=exp(1-1/[4(N+2)(-1-N)]) for -2<N<-1 and zero otherwise; psi is nonnegative C_c^infinity, nonzero, and delta derivatives vanish on it
declared_conventions.finite_part: <Pf_mu(1/|N|),phi>=lim_{epsilon->0+}[integral_{|N|>epsilon} phi(N)/|N| dN+2 phi(0) log(mu epsilon)] with nondimensionalized local N and mu>0
selection_family: absolute real-arm versus signed single-sheet punctured glue
positive finite-part reference scales mu in {1/2,1,2,4}
lower, upper, and principal-value signed boundary prescriptions
no imported parity, causal, determinant-line, BFV, or physical-cycle selection

controls: Exact arm restriction: K_abs=K_signed for N>0 and K_abs=-K_signed for N<0.
A nonnegative smooth probe supported inside (-2,-1) pairs strictly positively with K_abs-K_signed while every zero-supported contact term pairs to zero.
Scaling degree omega=1 equals lapse dimension d=1, so the same-scaling-degree extension freedom is order-zero point support c*delta, separately for the absolute and signed punctured distributions.
The declared finite-part definition obeys the exact +2*C*log(mu'/mu)*delta scale-change identity, checked numerically on an independent smooth compact probe.
Lower and upper lateral numerical boundary controls reproduce opposite plus/minus pi*C delta coefficients on an even Schwartz probe after the signed punctured glue has been chosen.

decision_table.condition: the kernels differ on a test supported away from zero and both critical-scaling extension families retain an order-zero contact parameter
the kernels agree away from zero but retain a contact parameter
the kernels agree as punctured distributions and a unique same-scaling-degree extension follows from the declared source data
any executable control or theorem hypothesis fails
